scenes.anchor_text:
In the shade of the house, in the sunshine of the riverbank near the boats, in
the shade of the Sal-wood forest, in the shade of the fig tree is where
Siddhartha grew up, the handsome son of the Brahman, the young falcon, together
with his friend Govinda, son of a Brahman.
scenes.scene_description: Young Siddhartha and Govinda explore the lush riverbank. The light filters through the trees, dappling the ground in sunlight and shadow.

scenes.anchor_text:
The sun tanned his light shoulders
by the banks of the river when bathing, performing the sacred ablutions, the
sacred offerings. In the mango grove, shade poured into his black eyes, when
playing as a boy, when his mother sang, when the sacred offerings were made, when his father, the scholar, taught him, when the wise men talked.

scenes.anchor_text:
For a long
time, Siddhartha had been partaking in the discussions of the wise men,
practising debate with Govinda, practising with Govinda the art of reflection,
the service of meditation. He already knew how to speak the Om silently, the
word of words, to speak it silently into himself while inhaling, to speak it
silently out of himself while exhaling, with all the concentration of his soul, the forehead surrounded by the glow of the clear-thinking spirit.
scenes.scene_description: Siddhartha meditates with Govinda in a serene outdoor space. Light illuminates his forehead.

scenes.anchor_text:
Love touched the hearts of the Brahmans’ young daughters when Siddhartha
walked through the lanes of the town with the luminous forehead, with the eye
of a king, with his slim hips.
scenes.scene_description: Siddhartha walks through the town's lanes, his presence noticed by the young women. Focus is on the architecture of the town and their reaction to him rather than a direct portrait.

scenes.anchor_text:
Walking the rosy paths of the fig tree garden, sitting in the bluish
shade of the grove of contemplation, washing his limbs daily in the bath ofepentance, sacrificing in the dim shade of the mango forest, his gestures of
perfect decency, everyone’s love and joy, he still lacked all joy in his
heart.

scenes.anchor_text:
Surely, many verses of the holy books, particularly in the Upanishades of
Samaveda, spoke of this innermost and ultimate thing, wonderful verses.
“Your soul is the whole world”, was written there, and it was
written that man in his sleep, in his deep sleep, would meet with his innermost
part and would reside in the Atman.

scenes.anchor_text:
“Govinda,” Siddhartha spoke to his friend, “Govinda, my dear,
come with me under the Banyan tree, let’s practise meditation.”
They went to the Banyan tree, they sat down, Siddhartha right here, Govinda
twenty paces away.
scenes.scene_description: Siddhartha and Govinda sit in meditation beneath a sprawling Banyan tree, its roots reaching down like ancient fingers.

scenes.anchor_text:
Thus sat he, wrapped up in contemplation, thinking Om, his soul
sent after the Brahman as an arrow.
Once, Samanas had travelled through Siddhartha’s town, ascetics on a
pilgrimage, three skinny, withered men, neither old nor young, with dusty and
bloody shoulders, almost naked, scorched by the sun, surrounded by loneliness, strangers and enemies to the world, strangers and lank jackals in the realm of humans.
scenes.scene_description: Siddhartha sits in deep meditation, his posture rigid. In the distance, the silhouettes of the Samanas approach the town.

scenes.anchor_text:
Siddhartha entered the chamber, where his father was sitting on a mat of bast,
and stepped behind his father and remained standing there, until his father
felt that someone was standing behind him. Quoth the Brahman: “Is that
you, Siddhartha? Then say what you came to say.”
scenes.scene_description: Siddhartha stands silently behind his father in a sparsely furnished chamber, lit by the moon. The tension is palpable.

scenes.anchor_text:
As he slowly left on stiff legs in the first light of day the still quiet town,
a shadow rose near the last hut, who had crouched there, and joined the
pilgrim—Govinda.
“You have come,” said Siddhartha and smiled.
“I have come,” said Govinda.
scenes.scene_description: Siddhartha leaves the town at dawn, Govinda emerging from the shadows to join him on his journey.
